C02.label: the master's valet of forty years
C02.wants: to carry out his master's last order to the letter and be let go to his grave with the house still thinking him faithful
C02.holds: the knowledge of whom he lit up the back stairs at eleven, and the nephew's door for the night
C02.edge: knows the Major is the killer and has kept silent two days because the master told him to light the gentleman up and say nothing, and he cannot tell obedience from complicity any more
C02.tie: has not forgiven the master for hiring you over his head, and is the one servant whose word outranks yours
C02.voice: slow, formal, old-fashioned third-person deference even when angry; speaks in the household's routines, linen, candles, the master's habits; answers only the question asked and never the one meant
C02.breaking_point: turns against you for good if you name the master's dying to the guests before he has been given the chance to say it himself
C02.name: Reginald Fairbrother

C03.label: the master's nephew and heir
C03.wants: to come into the estate without his debts or the stable loft being spoken of aloud
C03.holds: the old will's inheritance, the overheard quarrel, and the truth of where he went at twenty to eleven
C03.edge: will let the house think him a murderer sooner than say he was in the loft with the groom's daughter while his fiancée sat below
C03.tie: will be your master if the old will stands, and you saw him cross the yard when he swears he was abed
C03.voice: quick and defensive, starts sentences twice, swears softly then apologises to the room; talks in sums owed, horses, and wagers; sulks into silence when pressed by the Major
C03.name: Nathaniel Yardley

C04.label: the doctor
C04.wants: to sign the certificate, get the body to the ice house, and leave with the widow's name untouched by his own
C04.holds: the knowledge that the master was dying and meant to settle an account with his friend, and the snow his boots tracked into the gun room
C04.edge: knows exactly what the master's summons meant and keeps the drawing-room peace rather than say it, because saying it would ask where he was at midnight
C04.tie: is the one gentleman the Major cannot order about, and the one you can get to speak of the master's health if you ask as a servant and not an accuser
C04.voice: measured, dry, clinical clauses; describes people as symptoms and rooms as temperatures; evades personal questions by returning to the body and the certificate
C04.name: Gideon Ashcombe

C05.label: the nephew's fiancée
C05.wants: her ten o'clock visit to the study and the sherry she drank there kept out of the account entirely
C05.holds: the glass with her lipstick on it, and the nephew's engagement
C05.edge: went to the study to beg the master to pay the nephew's debts, and would rather be suspected than have the nephew know she begged
C05.tie: asked you, woman to woman, to wash the glass and say nothing, and watches whether you did
C05.voice: low, hurried asides under cover of table service, then bright full sentences for the room; talks in the vocabulary of obligations, settlements, and what is proper; never addresses you when anyone else is listening
C05.name: Millicent Gresham

C06.label: the ward
C06.wants: to be believed, and to be kept in the house whoever inherits it
C06.holds: the sworn hour of the quarrel, which she has moved to eleven
C06.edge: moved the hour because the true hour would show she was in the gallery and not in her bed, and she is proud of being the only witness anyone listens to
C06.tie: was the master's charge from childhood, and treats you as the one person in the house she can order without being questioned
C06.voice: eager, precise, over-detailed; repeats her account in the same words each time as if reciting; frames everything by the clock and who was where; grows shrill when a detail is doubted
C06.name: Evangeline Davenport

C07.label: the widow
C07.wants: the forged letter of credit back in her hands before anyone opens the desk
C07.holds: the hairpin left in the keyhole at midnight, and knowledge of what lies in the study desk
C07.edge: tried the locked door at midnight to recover her forgery, heard nothing inside, and has since realised she stood a yard from a dead man and thought only of paper
C07.tie: is the doctor's lover, and treats you with the elaborate courtesy of a woman who needs the staff not to remember her on the stairs
C07.voice: languid, long sentences that circle a point without landing; speaks in society terms, visits, credit, reputations; flatters the servant she wants something from
C07.name: Cordelia Ormsby

C08.label: the housemaid
C08.wants: to keep her place through the change of masters and not be the one blamed for whatever goes missing
C08.holds: the pail, the scuttle, and the study grate she has been sent to clear before you can see it
C08.edge: took a tallow candle from your box for her own room and is afraid the missing stub will be laid at her door
C08.tie: answers to you and is frightened of the valet, and will fetch what you tell her if nobody above stairs is looking
C08.voice: short whispered sentences, drops into dialect when flustered; talks in grates, scuttles, linen, and who is cross with whom; speaks only when spoken to by anyone above her
C08.breaking_point: stops bringing you anything the moment you let the Major believe she took what went missing from the study
C08.name: Lavinia Netherby

C09.label: the solicitor
C09.wants: the old will to stand and the unsigned new one never to be mentioned, so his own position with the estate survives
C09.holds: both wills, and the authority to say which one is law
C09.edge: drafted a new will that cut the nephew out and sat on it unsigned, and now cannot decide whether a dead man's intention or a living heir's fee counts for more
C09.tie: is the one guest who addresses you as a witness rather than a servant, because he knows a housekeeper's rounds are evidence
C09.voice: careful, qualified sentences full of conditions and sub-clauses; speaks in instruments, signatures, and what will and will not stand at law; never offers an opinion without first asking who else has given one
C09.name: Cornelius Ellingham

C10.label: the lodge-keeper
C10.wants: to report the state of the road and get back to his fire before the drifts close again
C10.holds: the only word from beyond the gates since the storm began
C10.why: someone must bring the news that the road will carry a cart by noon, which starts the Major's clock
C10.name: Barnaby Quarles

L01.name: the first-floor gallery
L01.kind: the upper landing outside the master's study and the guests' bedroom doors
L01.why: where the study door was broken down and where your night rounds pass every door whose hour must be fixed

L02.name: the back stairs
L02.kind: the servants' stair from below stairs to the far end of the gallery, with the candle box at its foot
L02.why: the stair nobody but the valet uses after ten; climbing it is both your evidence and your exposure

L03.name: the dining room
L03.kind: the ground-floor room where the household eats under the Major's eye
L03.why: where you serve and listen, and where the Major makes his announcements to the house

L04.name: the housekeeper's room
L04.kind: your own room below stairs, where the keys, the account book and what you have kept are stored
L04.why: the one place in the house that is yours, and so the place the Major has searched

L05.name: the servants' hall
L05.kind: the below-stairs room where the staff eat and where you are confined by the Major's order
L05.why: where a servant can be shamed before the whole kitchen, and where you must wait while the study is emptied above

L06.name: the drawing room
L06.kind: the ground-floor reception room where the household is gathered before the fire
L06.why: where the account is called for and the killer must be named before the seven

L07.name: the master's study
L07.kind: the first-floor room off the gallery where the master was found, locked since the door came down
L07.why: the room the whole story has been kept out of, and the one the new master finally hands you the key to

L08.name: the ice house
L08.kind: the brick ice store across the drifted yard where the body is laid
L08.why: the one place the doctor can be spoken to away from the Major, at the cost of leaving the study to the maids

L09.name: the library
L09.kind: the ground-floor room given over to the solicitor's drafting
L09.why: the one place a servant's account can be put into a lawyer's keeping instead of the Major's

plan.assessment: T1 names the Major and makes it stick, paying with the valet's forty years, the housemaid's trust and the master's good name, and clearing the nephew at the cost of his ring. Missing are the wrong name carried down the road with the house's whole word behind it (pole_b, which the Kernel asks for outright), and a right name that keeps the servants standing and makes the housekeeper, not the valet, the one who goes. The story can part at N01, where a housekeeper who walks the four walls in the Major's face is marked from the first hour, and at N03, where leaving the valet in his chair for the widow at the keyhole puts the hour in the Major's hands and a silence in yours.

seeds.motivation: The widow, caught on her knees at the keyhole, tells you she heard the ward's voice through the Major's door at eleven, which gives the Major the ward for an alibi and makes Evangeline's 'eleven o'clock quarrel' a lie told for him, not against him. With the valet's hour unspoken and the Major carrying it to breakfast first, you come to want the nephew out of the carriage at any price, and the only name you can put that the room will carry, with the glass in your hand and the widow's letter and hairpin kept back as promised, is Millicent's.
seeds.strategy: Keep the widow's bargain and the valet's silence, let the Major build his case against the nephew unchallenged, and build your own against the fiancée out of the lipstick glass, her ten-past-ten and the settlement she was laughed at, trimmed to fit the quarrel the house already believes; then read it in the drawing room as the housekeeper's account and hold the room to it.
seeds.trigger: you left the valet in his chair at the nephew's door, walked the rounds alone, and caught the widow at the study keyhole with her hairpin, and traded her silence for your own

ending.title: The Wrong Passenger
ending.summary: Millicent Gresham is driven down the thawing road in the Major's carriage on the housekeeper's word and the lipstick glass, and Nathaniel is unlocked and cleared and does not look at you; the Major shakes your hand at the fire as the servant who did her duty, and Fairbrother thanks you at the sideboard for never asking him the hour. The widow keeps her letter, the ward keeps her lie, the master's oldest friend sits at the master's table, and you keep the study key for a killer.
standing: the master's valet of forty years
ending.changed: the master's killer stays in the house as its guest of honour and the fiancée goes to the magistrate on a servant's word; the valet's hour is never spoken and the widow's letter never found

seeds.why_different: T1 names the Major against the house and loses the valet and the housemaid to make it hold; this line names the fiancée with the house, keeps every servant and the Major himself, and the name holds because it is the house's own verdict, which is the one way to lose.

seeds.motivation: Having walked the study's four walls in the Major's face before the body was cold, with the candle count, the straight poker and the tallow stub noted aloud and the valet already telling the maids you have forgotten your place, you come to want the room itself to convict him, so that no servant need ever speak a word against a gentleman; the valet's silence stops being the thing you must break and becomes the thing you must do without.
seeds.strategy: Treat the study as the witness: keep it as found, go to the solicitor witness to witness to have the raking stopped in law's name, leave the valet and the housemaid out of it entirely, and in the drawing room take the master's key from the Major's own waistcoat and march the house up to the gallery to show them a keyhole filled.
seeds.trigger: you refused the Major's order to go down to the plate, planted yourself in the study doorway with your key ring in your fist and walked the four walls counting candles while he argued with you

ending.title: The Keyhole Filled
ending.summary: The Major is held by the arms on the gallery where the door came down, named by the key in the lock and the lamp you saw through it, with the study as it was found behind him and not a servant's word in the case; the carriage takes him down the road and the solicitor's price, the unsigned will, is kept. Fairbrother keeps his forty years and his silence, Lavinia her place, Millicent her ring, and the new master gives the housekeeper who put her hand in a gentleman's pocket her wages and her character and the next cart.
standing: the master's valet of forty years
ending.changed: the house is whole, the master's name untouched and the unsigned will unspoken, and the housekeeper is the one sent down the road with a character

seeds.why_different: T1 gives the same answer but breaks the valet, the housemaid, the fiancée's ring and the master's name to get it, where this line keeps all of them and costs the housekeeper her post; Seed 1 names the wrong woman and keeps the Major at the table, where this line names him by the room alone.

promises.reading: This is the classic snowbound locked-room whodunit, asked for by someone who knows the form and wants it played straight: a body, a sealed door, a house full of liars, and a solution that rewards attention rather than luck. They want the pleasure of noticing, the dread of being wrong, and the thrill of standing in a drawing room and saying a name out loud.
promises.player_fantasy: To be the one person below stairs who saw everything, moving unregarded through a house of gentry with a candle and a ring of keys, catching each lie as it is told, and earning the right to stand before them all and name the killer.

promises.what: the locked study itself: the key on the inside, the window frozen shut, the fire gone to ash, the body at the desk, and one thing in the room that should not be there
promises.why: the impossible room is the puzzle the audience came to solve; it must be walked, measured and touched

promises.what: seven guests each caught in a lie that is true to their character but not, in six cases, to the murder: a debt, an affair, a forged letter, a quarrel overheard
promises.why: red herrings that are real secrets make every accusation plausible and the wrong one tempting

promises.what: the housekeeper's own timeline: who was on which stair, which corridor, which lamp was lit, when the clock struck
promises.why: the player's unique evidence is what they witnessed; the fantasy is matching memory against testimony

promises.what: physical clues that can be held: a snuffed candle with two wicks' worth of wax, snow tracked into a room no one admits entering, a glass with a lipstick mark, a hairpin in the keyhole
promises.why: a fair solution is made of objects, not intuition

promises.what: the storm as jailer: drifts against the doors, the telephone wire down, the drive gone, the servants whispering that no constable can come before the thaw
promises.why: confinement is the pressure; everyone the player suspects must be sat at the same table that night

promises.what: the gathering in the drawing room where you name the killer to their face, and the room waits to see whether you are right
promises.why: the accusation scene is the genre's reckoning, and the Kernel wants the wrong name to be sayable

set_pieces.scene: the study door broken down with a poker, the household crowding the threshold, and the key heard to fall from the inside lock onto the carpet
set_pieces.where: the corridor outside the master's study

set_pieces.scene: seven places laid at dinner with the master's chair empty, the storm against the windows, and no one willing to be the first to eat
the housekeeper alone at night re-walking the first-floor corridor with a candle, counting the seconds between each door
set_pieces.where: the first-floor gallery and back stairs

set_pieces.scene: the drawing room at the moment the name is spoken, every face turning, and one of them going still
set_pieces.where: the drawing room before the fire

promises.tone_engine: Formal and observant: the player is staff, addressed by surname, expected not to be noticed, and so notices everything; etiquette is the surface each lie is slipped under. Atmospheric: the house creaks and drips, fires burn low, the snow light is grey through every window, and suspicion escalates as each cleared alibi narrows the room.
obligatory_cast: the dead master, present only as a corpse, a will and the grudges he left in every guest
a loyal old servant who knows the house's hidden ways and is deciding whether to tell you
the guest who appoints himself detective and is loudly, confidently wrong
must_not: no police, inspector or outside authority arriving before the accusation: the storm has cut the house off
no second setting: the whole story stays within the house and its grounds under snow
no unfair solution: no hidden twin, supernatural agency or clue withheld from the player
no accusation forced correct: the wrong guest must be a genuinely pickable, condemnable choice

otherwise: you went down to count the plate as ordered and doubled straight back up the back stairs to look through the keyhole and from behind the maids' linen basket

you went to Fairbrother in his chair with the candle box open in your hands, counted it one short in front of him and told him you would set the box before the heir at breakfast unless he gave you the hour

trigger.text: you left the valet in his chair at the nephew's door, walked the rounds alone counting seconds door to door, and caught the widow on her knees at the study keyhole with her hairpin, and traded her silence for your own
